Hi John — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a short runbook and a sanitized CSV sample. See attachments: admin_activity_export_instructions.pdf, sample_admin_trace.csv.

Quick summary (high level):
- Events captured: console auth attempts (success/fail), SSO events (IdP assertions), API token creations/revocations, RBAC changes (role assignments, policy updates), model/version deployments and rollbacks, route changes, resource scaling events, operator-initiated job cancellations, audit-config changes, and exports/exports-requests themselves.

- Retention: Hosted (default 365 days), Dedicated (configurable between 90d–7 years depending on contract), Private (customer-managed; we provide export tooling and snapshot scripts). Retention extensions for Hosted can be purchased as an add-on; we also support long-term archival to S3.

- Export options: ad-hoc JSON/CSV exports via Console; scheduled delivery to customer-owned S3 buckets; streaming to customer Splunk/Datadog/Elastic pipelines via our log-forwarder; bulk snapshot exports (ndjson) for auditor handoff; BigQuery connector available for enterprise Dedicated customers. Exports are time-bounded and support filtered queries by actor, resource, and action.

- PII/redaction: exported traces include user_id and resource_id hashed by default for Hosted exports. For Dedicated/Private we can provide raw IDs under an approved SOC2-data-access workflow. Redaction rules can be applied at export time (strip request/response bodies, truncate tokens, or pseudonymize emails).

- Auditor snapshot process: see attached runbook (admin_activity_export_instructions.pdf). TL;DR: 1) create export job in Console -> choose time range and hash/raw policy, 2) set destination (S3 or enable temporary console download), 3) request customer-signed data access form (if raw IDs requested), 4) we deliver a signed manifest + SHA256 checksums.

I'll let Connor add technical runbook steps and logging schema. If you want Redwood to produce the snapshot directly, we can commit to a one-time export and provide a signed manifest — let me know which retention/PII level you need.

Best,

John — adding technical details you can share with your auditor. Attachment: export_runbook.md (runbook excerpt below).

Runbook excerpt (sanitized):
1) Console export (quick): Console -> Security -> Admin Activity -> New Export. Select UTC time window, choose fields (timestamp, actor, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id_hash, ip, user_agent, request_id), choose delivery (temporary download or S3). Exports are ndjson compressed as .ndjson.gz.

2) S3 delivery (recommended for >7 days): Provide an s3-bucket ARN and IAM role. We will deliver to prefix redwood-audit-exports/<account>/<YYYYMMDD>/. Each file includes a manifest.json and checksum file.

3) Splunk/Elastic streaming: configure endpoint + token; we support TLS and HMAC signing of batches. Throughput is autoscaled; ordering is best-effort.

4) Snapshot integrity: every export includes manifest (job_id, timeframe, field_schema_v, record_count) and SHA256 per file. We recommend checking manifest + SHA before ingestion.

5) Redaction knobs: export field filter, redact_payload flag, email_hashing (salted SHA256), ip-truncate (v4/v6).

6) Retention config: hosted.default_retention_days=365; custom_retention_flag available for enterprise via contract. For Dedicated, admins can set retention policy in the cluster config; for Private we provide the snapshot tooling and scripts.

Note: SIG/CAIQ question mapping — the exported fields align to standard audit items: user authentication events (SIG ID A.1), admin action history (A.2), and data export controls (A.6). I can generate a small mapping table if helpful.

—Connor O'Brien

John — answers and next steps, pulling Grace in for legal/data-access approvals:  

Answers: 
- 24-month retention on Hosted: we can produce a one-time 24-month archival export for Hosted customers as a paid evidence package (includes ndjson snapshot, signed manifest, and export statement). Ongoing retention to 24 months on Hosted requires a retention add-on or migration to Dedicated.

- IdP assertions: the standard export includes IdP assertion reference fields (assertion_id, idp_subject_hash, auth_time). Full SAML assertion payloads are classified as sensitive; we can include assertion_id + timestamp + subject_hash in exports by default. If your auditor requires raw SAML assertions, that is treated as a restricted data request and requires an executed Data Access Agreement (attached link).

- Zip snapshot to S3: yes — we can schedule a single zipsnap for the 24-month window, deliver to your S3 prefix, and provide manifest + SHA256. Timeline: we can generate within 5 business days of an executed request and receipt of the S3 write role.
